intent: Shift sensor y-positions forward by +0.005 from the previous iteration (from y = 0.055, 0.035, 0.015, 0.035, 0.055 to y = 0.06, 0.04, 0.02, 0.04, 0.06) to improve early line detection and control anticipation, building on prior improvements. Retain sensor size at 0.016 and wheel track at 0.16 to maintain noise robustness and turning stability. Expect this fine adjustment to reduce line loss events and steering oscillations further, improving progress and completion on both oval and s-bend tracks, supporting better generalization.
rationale: Integrator feedback and telemetry show that despite previous increases in sensor size and wheel track and forward shifts of sensor y-positions, line loss events still occur once per run, causing off-track terminations. The controller compensates with moderate base speed and gains but cannot fully prevent line loss. A further small forward shift of sensor y-positions by +0.005 is a fine-tuning step to detect the line earlier and improve control anticipation without destabilizing sensor weighting. Retaining sensor size and wheel track preserves noise robustness and turning stability. This incremental change is expected to reduce line loss events and steering oscillations, improving control smoothness and completion rates as supported by telemetry evidence.
